description: Protocol-owned cross-field invariant inventory for Epic 2 intake and receipt prerequisites. Each item records the JavaScript and Rust validation surfaces that enforce or exercise the invariant.

invariants.summary: Coverage Mode must align with snippet policy, retention policy, evidence categories, warnings, and limitations.
Outbound Manifest remains local preview only: preview_generated, send_ready=false, local_only=true, approval_state=not_requested.
manifest_id is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical manifest content excluding manifest_id.
content_path values are portable, relative, slash-separated, anchored, and never host-local absolute paths or traversal forms.
Approved or declined decisions preserve the manifest identity and the context displayed before approval.
Bundle manifests require approved customer approval and remain not_submitted until future intake creates receipt states.
evidence_bundle_id is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical bundle manifest content excluding evidence_bundle_id.
Every bundle artifact reference is verified against copied bytes for digest and size before signing output is finalized.
Signature envelopes sign typed manifest or evidence bundle identities and keep synthetic/demo signing limitations explicit.
Local runner attempts preserve local failure/rerun/trust states and never introduce submitted, received, finalized, receipt, or attestation claims.
Real Raw Snippets and targeted files are rejected unless environment readiness explicitly permits them and all required readiness controls are true.
vendor_receipt_id is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical receipt identity input excluding vendor_receipt_id, receipt_signature, and repeated signed_identity metadata.
Vendor Receipt signatures reuse the common signature envelope with signed_identity_type vendor_receipt and signed_identity equal to vendor_receipt_id.
Approved-vs-received comparison rows and artifact count summaries must match before a received_with_receipt state exists.
Rejected or quarantined submissions must not be represented as Vendor Receipt records.
Receipt public verification metadata preserves historical key id/version and event-append hints without rewriting old receipt records.

New review state is only a newly appended event: sequence_number is strictly greater than every earlier sequence_number, no prior event is rewritten, reordered, or removed, event ids are unique, and a repeated idempotency_key is an append no-op.

event_id equals the sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical event content excluding event_id, and identity_input_excludes is exactly ["event_id"], so events serialize deterministically for future hash chaining or transparency-log projection.

checkpoint_id equals the sha256 of RFC 8785 canonical checkpoint content excluding checkpoint_id, deployment identity is explicit, and the Merkle root commits the deployment-wide set of per-review chain heads without changing review events.

Corrections are expressed only through supersedes_event_id pointing at an earlier event in the same log; customer-authored events, regardless of event_type, must not supersede an expert classification_recorded event.

Every event declares exactly one visibility, internal_note may appear only on internal_only events, and the customer-facing projection omits internal_only events entirely while preserving event_type, event_timestamp, actor_category, artifact_refs, and reason when present.

A customer projection is exactly the customer_facing subset of its review event log, in sequence_number order, with per-entry fields carried through unchanged: it may neither omit a customer_facing event (truncation) nor contain an entry the log never recorded (fabrication).

Every stored object declares exactly one retention/source-derived class; log_or_trace, analytics_record, crash_report, and support_attachment kinds may only be never_collected or retained_review_artifact, and customer_opt_in_retained_source is only permitted under environment_profile partner_pilot_real_snippet_ready.

Deletion is an append-only evidence_deleted event that references a Deletion Evidence artifact and declares its source_derived_class; a status label with no deletion_evidence_ref is not a receipt of deletion.

Sensitive artifact inspection appends an evidence_accessed event carrying actor, timestamp, artifact references, tenant/review access scope, and purpose where available; access outside the actor tenant/review scope is denied and emits no event implying inspection occurred.

An appended evidence lifecycle event has a sequence_number strictly greater than every sequence_number already present, never reuses an event_id, and never rewrites, reorders, or removes an existing event; a repeated idempotency_key is an append no-op.

A retention opt-in record declares source_derived_class customer_opt_in_retained_source, a customer approval reference, the retained artifact identities (all schema-required), and a retention period whose end_timestamp is after its start_timestamp (validateRetentionOptInRecordSemantics). The record carries no environment_profile field, so the partner_pilot_real_snippet_ready gate is enforced where the profile is known: recordOptInRetention takes it as a parameter, and classifyStoredObject enforces it per stored object.

retained_finding, retained_metadata, retained_attestation, retained_customer_opt_in_snippet, deleted_transient, and never_collected stay visibly distinct, each pinned to exactly one source-derived class; one artifact_ref may not appear under two different categories; and every deleted_transient entry resolves to a Deletion Evidence reference rather than a dangling one.

The three intake outcomes stay mutually exclusive and complete: received_with_receipt requires a minted vendor receipt reference and carries no failure reason codes, rejected_no_receipt and quarantined_no_receipt each carry at least one reason code and no receipt reference, next_path may only be one the state can offer, and failure copy stays claim-safe so it never implies CodeAttest reviewed or accepted the evidence.

Rejected and quarantined submission outcomes are recorded as submission_rejected or submission_quarantined events in the existing review-event-log; each event references its submission-outcome artifact, derives idempotency_key from (bundle_instance_id, submission_attempt_id), and relies on appendReviewEvent to keep distinct retries append-only without a second history artifact.

Review Finding Draft normalization requires a received Vendor Receipt and preserves the matched evidence bundle, manifest, and source scanner finding set identities; rejected, quarantined, or no-receipt inputs are not normalizable.

Scanner findings are normalized only into draft review artifacts: candidate ids, scanner sources, rule ids, severity, confidence, affected areas, and evidence references remain provenance and cannot create expert classifications, remediation guidance, attestation copy, receipt semantics, or scanner execution fields.

Coverage Mode and evidence basis are explicit on each draft, threshold gaps are required for scanner-only, metadata-only, deleted, not-submitted, never-collected, or unresolved evidence, and deleted-under-policy source-derived content renders only as deleted with deletion evidence rather than available content.

No-findings normalization emits no drafts, uses the exact statement "No findings were produced by the configured inputs", and carries an explicit limitation that this does not prove absence of vulnerabilities.

Reviewer classification records may only use the allowed taxonomy: likely, confirmed, inconclusive, or requires_customer_side_validation. Scanner, remediation, validation, accepted-risk, false-positive, and Attestation states are not classification values.

Reviewer classification records and classification_recorded events may only be authored by CodeAttest reviewer actors. Customer-authored workflow, remediation, accepted-risk, validation, and other non-reviewer events cannot create or rewrite expert classification history.

A confirmed classification requires meaningful confirmation criteria and rationale; whenever any evidence basis is scanner, metadata, unavailable, not-submitted, never-collected, or unresolved evidence, defensible confirmation criteria must explain why the threshold is crossed. The evidence_basis must be bound to the referenced draft evidence refs and must not contradict source_reference_state.

A requires_customer_side_validation classification must carry a meaningful validation path summary or a claim-safe validation path reference, so customer-side validation is visible as a required path rather than an empty label.

Classification updates are appended as classification_recorded events referencing typed classification artifacts; updates use supersedes_event_id or prior classification record references, and previous history remains visible rather than being overwritten.

Classification rationale, criteria, threshold gaps, limitations, validation-path summaries, and validation-path refs must not carry raw source bytes, raw scanner stdout/stderr, secrets, token-like strings, or claim-unsafe assurance copy.

Reviewer remediation guidance uses bounded statuses. Actionable guidance requires meaningful remediation and validation steps, limitations, evidence references, and exploitability rationale for likely/confirmed classification context; limited or unavailable guidance requires an insufficient-evidence reason plus a next step or validation handoff.
Remediation guidance free text must not carry raw source bytes, scanner stdout/stderr, secrets, token-like strings, or claim-unsafe assurance and absence-of-vulnerabilities copy.

Customer remediation status records capture customer owner/status/due-date/target-state/notes and export posture as audit metadata without rewriting expert classification or reviewer remediation rationale; accepted-risk and false-positive states are excluded from this vocabulary.

Customer-facing finding records keep expert classification, evidence basis, reviewer guidance, customer remediation metadata, verification state, and later accepted-risk/false-positive visibility separate; one ambiguous status field is invalid and hidden customer notes are not exported.

Reviewer remediation guidance is recorded as remediation_guidance_recorded and customer status as customer_remediation_recorded, both referencing typed artifacts through the append-only review event log; customer-authored events cannot supersede classification_recorded or remediation_guidance_recorded chains, including multi-hop chains.
javascript_coverage: review-event-log customer supersedes remediation guidance fixture

invariants.summary: Validation paths keep remote dynamic testing, customer-run scripts, and manual steps distinct; remote testing requires authorization and safety assumptions, and customer-run script paths require explicit reviewer validation script refs.

Reviewer validation scripts are either included base-package scripts with slot 1..3 or additional-script candidates with pricing TBD and no included slot; builders enforce the cap with prior included-script context.

Validation paths and reviewer validation scripts are recorded with validation_recorded events using exact singleton artifact refs and reviewer actor authority; customer events cannot supersede validation path or script chains.

Validation path and reviewer script text, command/script content, and customer-facing projections use the shared normalized source/claim-safety matcher and cannot carry source-text markers or claim-unsafe assurance copy.
Accepted-risk and false-positive records are separate retained outcome artifacts and are not classification values or customer remediation statuses.

False-positive records require reviewer rationale, evidence basis, limitations, actor/timestamp, and finding/classification refs; customer-facing projections keep the finding visible with a record-backed outcome section.

Accepted risk requires customer rationale/sign-off evidence, may coexist with remediation/validation history, and cannot imply remediation, verification, auditor/control acceptance, certification, regulator approval, independent assurance, or absence of vulnerabilities.

Verification pass scope records customer-selected findings with customer actor or explicit customer-backed selection provenance; reviewer/vendor/service actors cannot silently choose findings for the customer.
Selected findings preserve normalized Review Finding draft, classification, remediation/status, validation path/script, and outcome refs without rewriting prior Story 3 artifacts.
Included verification pass availability is bounded to 30 days and included Validation Script allocation is capped at unique slots 1..3 while additional scripts are pricing TBD candidates.
Story 4.1 scope selection cannot carry follow-up evidence, before/after outcomes, verification-complete status, Attestation/addendum content, or unsafe full-review success copy.

Verification scope changes append verification_scope_recorded events with exact singleton scope artifact refs; corrections supersede only prior verification-scope events and never classification/remediation/validation/outcome chains.
Verification evidence remains metadata-only, customer/customer-backed, bound to active scope and formal commit/path/script context, with lifecycle-safe artifacts and versioned append-only events.

Verification decisions are reviewer-owned, semantically revalidate evidence, preserve original basis, cover every recorded criterion, and emit canonical actionable outcomes through versioned append-only events.

Standalone addenda preserve selected scope and commit, resolve each evidence record exactly once, require deletion lifecycle proof, use active decision/evidence event heads, and keep incomplete outcomes not finalized.

Attestation sections preserve retained scope, method, receipt, finding, remediation, verification, lifecycle, limitation, and supporting-reference context without assurance conclusions or source content.
Only approved versioned SOC 2 supporting-evidence, generic technology-risk, or customer-review mappings are customer-facing; consumer decision authority and non-acceptance language remain explicit.

Static manifests preserve stable bundle identity, versioned content identity, file digests, Evidence Bundle representation, minimization disposition, and offline verification while excluding internal pilot learning.
Static portal projections expose fixed document navigation, offline search/print/copy capability, relative links, and no remote assets, analytics, live API, or runtime authorization dependency.
Only a customer actor finalizes or exports after visible context and verified prerequisites, producing a newly signed higher manifest version rather than mutating generated bytes.
Pilot metrics and feedback are bounded content-free internal-only records and events that are excluded from Attestation, static manifest, portal, search, print, and customer event history.

A final partner-pilot gate references one approved, managed-key-signed, content-addressed decision over its exact approval input; that decision binds exactly one fresh passing independently reviewed evidence record for each of the seven controls and the exact pilot release and deployment digests.
